_doc: UIUX-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-17): the UI/UX manager is a closed loop in code. QNFO's front end barely changed while its back end moved, and it drifted into a mishmash; this loop makes that impossible by auditing every front-end surface on a clock, walking the user paths as executable tests, reading first-party path analytics, running pre-registered A/B experiments on path steps with automatic promotion, and filing a fix item for every failed audit or fallen path that the self-coding agent works and the loop re-probes. Read by foundation/uiux.py; browser half in scripts/uiux_audit.mjs (Playwright, free tier, run by .github/workflows/uiux.yml and by any cloud session); checked by `python3 -m foundation uiux --check`. Its two essential variables (ui_findings, happy_paths) are declared in doctrine/ultrastability.json so the slow loop can restructure when they stay out of bounds. Never relax a rule or a budget to clear a finding: fix the page, or change this file by PR with a lineage note.

surfaces._doc: Every origin a person can land on. io, org and app come from doctrine/stakeholders.json domains plus the app host; tenant and spinoff apps come from ops/spinoff/ledger.jsonl (live, not retired). The offline audit renders the site Worker in-process; --live audits the real hosts.

audits._doc: kind -> severity. blocking findings count against the ui_findings variable; warnings are filed as items on repeat but do not move the slow loop.

boundary._doc: USER-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY: a person sees their idea and the front end. Backend detail (storage names, queue ids, stack traces, raw nulls) never reaches a user page. Engineer and owner lanes are named exempt, each with its reason.

exempt_paths./engineers: the engineer lane lists every capability and its trigger by design
exempt_paths./claims: the claims register names probes and files
exempt_paths./roadmap: the public roadmap names item ids
exempt_paths./org: the organisation map names loops and files
exempt_paths./dashboard: tenant dashboard for the owner of that tenant

structure._doc: Page invariants every user page keeps (DESIGN-LANGUAGE-1 core): one h1, a lang attribute, a viewport meta, a title, no empty links or buttons, at most one primary action.

copy._doc: Copy lint on user pages: placeholders and unfinished text. Claims drift is checked by foundation/claims.py and counted as its own kind.

performance._doc: Size and structure budgets measured offline (HTML bytes, DOM nodes, inline script bytes); --live adds real navigation timing against the same loop.

visual._doc: Visual-regression without storing images: each page at each width is fingerprinted by the rounded boxes and computed colour/type tokens of its headings, links, buttons, inputs and landmarks, and compared with ops/uiux/baseline.json. A page below min_similarity is drift; an intended redesign re-baselines in the same PR (`node scripts/uiux_audit.mjs --rebaseline`).
visual._baseline_roll: DECLARED-LIVE-1: a baseline older than max_baseline_days rolls forward after the weekly comparison (--roll-baseline in uiux.yml), so drift is measured against the previous window, never against a week-old snapshot.

paths._doc: User paths come from doctrine/stakeholders.json: each audience's entry page (/for/<id>) and its ordered steps. extra holds paths that are not an audience's (the idea-to-start happy path). Funnel completion = share of a day's visitors who reached the entry and then each later step in order, read from first-party hits (a visitor id rotates daily, so a path is measured within one day).

experiments._doc: A/B experiments on path steps reuse doctrine/design-experiments.json (pre-registered metric, guards, sample, no peeking). An experiment with a `slot` is served by site/worker.js from site/uiux-data.js (generated); exposure is one first-party event `exp:<id>:<arm>` per visitor-day; conversion is the visitor reaching `convert_on` after exposure. The loop evaluates running experiments with design.evaluate, promotes a kept arm into `defaults` (served as the new control) and records the verdict, or leaves the control.
